about: Units of pronunciation that Preference Grammar compares, the realisations to test for in the audio, and the reference judgements for the knowledge-based tenets (I-Ac; Ped-C lists). The PG sources assign these by expert judgement; entries marked provisional are defaults chosen from the cited literature and must be confirmed by the PG experts.

TH-voiceless.label: <th>
TH-voiceless.notes: I-Ac: the Lingua Franca Core treats /θ/ as non-core and lists [t], [f] and [s] as substitutes without choosing; stopping ([t], [t̪]) is an established norm in Irish, Caribbean and Liberian English and in ICAO radiotelephony ('tree' for three), TH-fronting ([f]) in London English. No L1-variety norm uses [s] or [z]. This reproduces Ugorji's operability table for 'think'. ICE-Nigeria word-initial /θ/: [θ] 47%, [t] 49%, [s] 4% (Oyebola, Ho & Li 2019).

validation.note: kappa 0.68 on 85 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

TH-voiced.label: <th>
TH-voiced.notes: Provisional: by analogy with /θ/ (LFC non-core; stopping established in Irish, Caribbean and Liberian English; fronting in London English). Nigerian realisations: [d] in the South, [z] among Hausa speakers when reading (Udofot; Muhammad-Gombe 2019).

validation.note: kappa 0.64 on 129 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

NURSE.label: NURSE
NURSE.notes: The NURSE quality is part of the Lingua Franca Core. Nigerian English measurements (9 Igbo speakers): [ɛ] 40%, [a] 31%, [ɔ] 16%, [ɜ] 8%, [e] 5%, largely spelling-led (Jamakovic & Fuchs 2019). Ugorji's national model: model з/ε; developmental ε/a/з.

validation.note: kappa 0.23 on 86 tokens from 21 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

STRUT.label: STRUT
STRUT.notes: Provisional international list (RP/GA qualities). Nigerian English: [ɔ] (basic Southern), [a] (basic Hausa), [ʌ] at the sophisticated level (Jowitt 2019: 41 via Udofot); national model ʌ/ɒ.

KIT.label: KIT
KIT.notes: Provisional. Vowel length (KIT vs FLEECE) is core in the LFC. Nigerian English realises KIT and FLEECE alike as [i] (Jamakovic & Fuchs 2019); national model ɪ, developmental ɪ/i.

validation.note: kappa 0.55 on 112 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

FLEECE.label: FLEECE
FLEECE.notes: Provisional. Nigerian English [i]; national model i.

validation.note: kappa 0.06 on 183 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

GOAT.label: GOAT
GOAT.notes: Ugorji (2010) evaluates /o/, /əʊ/, /ɒ/ for GOAT: /o/ wins with no violations; /əʊ/ violates FreQ, Pho-S, Ped-C; /ɒ/ violates I-Ac, ContR, FreQ, DisaM (Jowitt 2015: 8). Ugorji's /ɒ/ is phonetically [ɔ]. Monophthongal GOAT is an established norm in Scottish, Irish, Welsh and Northern English (provisional: check Wells 1982). Measured Nigerian English: [o] 50%, [ɔ] 16% (Jamakovic & Fuchs 2019); /o/ 91% (Eka 1985).

validation.note: kappa 0.16 on 68 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)

FACE.label: FACE
FACE.notes: Provisional. Monophthongal FACE is an established norm in Scottish, Irish, Welsh and Northern English. Nigerian English [e] about 51% (Jamakovic & Fuchs 2019); /e/ about 95% (Eka 1985); Jowitt proposes /e/ for Nigerian RP; national model e/eɪ.

validation.note: kappa 0.13 on 89 tokens from 22 Nigerian speakers (Speech Accent Archive; one paragraph, so new words are untested)
